raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Llama32Detector.parse_streaming_increment` emits **at most one unit per delta**:
a tool name with empty parameters, then that call's argument diff, then the next
call. A delta that carries one or more *complete* tool calls therefore leaves
work pending for the following delta, and when that delta was the last one
nothing ever picks it up. On `main`, streaming a call that completes inside a
single delta loses data that `detect_and_parse` returns:

```python
from sglang.srt.function_call.llama32_detector import Llama32Detector

text = (
    '<|python_tag|>{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Paris"}}'
    ';{"name": "get_tourist_attractions", "parameters": {"city": "Paris"}}'
)
d = Llama32Detector()
d.parse_streaming_increment(text, tools)   # -> name "get_weather", parameters ""
d.finish(tools)                            # -> nothing
# observed: one call, with EMPTY arguments, and the second call missing entirely
# expected: both calls with {"city": "Paris"}  (what detect_and_parse returns)
```

This is reachable whenever a tool call completes inside one delta: multi-token
deltas from speculative decoding / MTP, `stream_interval > 1`, or a call short
enough to be produced in a single step. The client either receives an unusable
`tool_call` with empty `arguments`, or no second call at all.

## Modifications

`finish()` now re-runs the incremental parser with an empty delta until a round
yields neither calls nor text, which releases everything the last delta left
pending. This is the pattern `GigaChat35Detector.finish()` already uses.

- `python/sglang/srt/function_call/llama32_detector.py`: +34
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py`: +46

The drain loop is bounded (`_MAX_FINISH_DRAIN_ROUNDS`) because each round
releases at most one unit, and it stops early once a round is empty, so a stream
that was already fully flushed returns nothing and no existing behavior changes.

### Scope

Other detectors defer the same way; I kept this PR to the Llama 3.2 detector
because it is the case I could validate end to end. A deliberately broader
attempt (draining inside `BaseFormatDetector.finish()`) was discarded: it
surfaces format-specific leftovers such as Mistral's array tail and a stray
`</tool_call>` as visible text, which needs per-format handling rather than a
blanket default (`Spark25Detector` and `KimiK3Detector` already drop such
residue in their own `finish()`).

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — parser-only change, no model forward or kernel code touched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — `finish()` runs once per request when the stream ends.

## Checklist

- [x] Format: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean; the only findings on
      both files are pre-existing and unchanged (`E722` x3 in the detector,
      `F841` x6 in the test file, identical before and after).
- [x] Unit tests:
  - `test_finish_releases_calls_that_completed_in_one_delta` — **bug regression**:
    fails on `main`, passes with the fix
  - `test_finish_is_a_noop_when_nothing_is_pending` — guards the stop condition
- [ ] Documentation: N/A

### Verification

```
pytest test/registered/unit/function_call test/registered/unit/parser
# 1063 passed, 1793 subtests passed  (1061 before this change)

pytest ... -k "finish_releases_calls or finish_is_a_noop_when_nothing"
# with fix:     2 passed
# fix reverted: 1 failed, 1 passed
```

I also replayed every tool-call string the existing suite feeds to
`detect_and_parse` (250 samples) through the streaming path at many chunk sizes
and compared against the non-streaming result: for the Llama 3.2 detector the
divergent cases drop from 11 to 3, with no new divergence for any other
detector.

---

Disclosure: prepared with AI assistance (DeepSeek Harness). All tests,
reproductions and the pre/post-fix comparison above were executed locally.

Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #38027015292](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38027015292)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->

<!-- pr-states:end -->

---

**Reviewer note — why the drain sits in `finish()` and not in the base class.**

There is an open base-class fix for part of this defect class (#32167, "Fix streaming tool calls losing arguments when completed in the final delta"). It does not cover this detector, and the reason is worth recording before anyone has to ask:

- The shared flush path is `FunctionCallParser.parse_stream_end()` -> `detector.finish()`, and **both** streaming entrypoints call it (`serving_chat.py:3030`, `serving_responses.py:2399`). The flush that #32167 extends, `_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args`, exists only in `serving_chat.py` (defined at 3115, used at 945); `serving_responses.py` has no equivalent.
- `BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment` processes exactly **one** JSON object per call — there is no loop between the `bot_token` search and the Case 1 / Case 2 returns. A delta carrying several complete calls therefore leaves the rest buffered, and registering the single object that was parsed does not recover them; the drain here re-runs the parser until it yields nothing, which does.
- `Llama32Detector.parse_streaming_increment` is an override that delegates parsing to `super()` (line 23), so a base-class change does reach this detector's *parsing* — but not the pending-call recovery, for the entrypoint reason above.

---

**Duplicate check (required before writing code).**

Searched open and draft PRs by file path, class name and defect description. The
closest competitor is **#32167** ("Fix streaming tool calls losing arguments when
completed in the final delta"), which patches the shared `BaseFormatDetector`; the
reason this detector-level fix is not subsumed by it is in the reviewer note above
(`GigaChat3Detector.parse_streaming_increment` never delegates to `super()`, and the
base parses one object per increment without draining the buffer).

Adjacent but distinct PRs touching the same shared test file — #28845 (Llama32
truncating text after the final call), #29582 (single quotes inside JSON values in
Llama32 streaming), #40291/#40295 (LFM2), #40741 (qwen3_coder) — address different
defects in different detectors; none of them drains a detector's pending calls at
stream end.

detail.title: [Fix] function_call: Flush pending tool calls at end of stream in the Llama 3.2 detector

files.patch:
@@ -8,12 +8,17 @@
 from sglang.srt.function_call.core_types import (
     StreamingParseResult,
     StructureInfo,
+    ToolCallItem,
     _GetInfoFunc,
 )
 from sglang.srt.function_call.utils import safe_literal_eval
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
+# Upper bound for the end-of-stream drain: each round releases at most one
+# pending unit (a tool name or one argument diff).
+_MAX_FINISH_DRAIN_ROUNDS = 1024
+
 
 class Llama32Detector(BaseFormatDetector):
     """
@@ -136,6 +141,35 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
             self._buffer = original_buffer
             return super().parse_streaming_increment(new_text, tools)
 
+    def finish(self, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult:
+        """Release tool-call state that the last delta left pending.
+
+        parse_streaming_increment emits at most one unit per call: a tool name
+        with empty parameters, then that call's argument diff, then the next
+        call. A delta that contains one or more complete tool calls therefore
+        leaves work pending for the following delta -- and when that delta was
+        the last one (multi-token deltas from speculative decoding / MTP,
+        ``stream_interval > 1``, or a call short enough to be generated in a
+        single step) nothing ever picks it up. Before this override the client
+        received the call with empty arguments, and a second call in the same
+        delta was dropped entirely, while detect_and_parse returned both.
+
+        Re-running the parser with an empty delta drains that queue. The loop
+        stops as soon as a round yields neither calls nor text, so a stream
+        that was already flushed returns nothing.
+        """
+        normal_parts: List[str] = []
+        calls: List[ToolCallItem] = []
+        for _ in range(_MAX_FINISH_DRAIN_ROUNDS):
+            result = self.parse_streaming_increment("", tools)
+            if not result.calls and not result.normal_text:
+                break
+            if result.normal_text:
+                normal_parts.append(result.normal_text)
+            if result.calls:
+                calls.extend(result.calls)
+        return StreamingParseResult(normal_text="".join(normal_parts), calls=calls)
+
     def structure_info(self) -> _GetInfoFunc:
         return lambda name: StructureInfo(
             begin='<|python_tag|>{"name":"' + name + '", "arguments":',

@@ -1307,6 +1307,100 @@ def test_with_python_tag_prefix(self):
         self.assertEqual(len(result.calls), 1)
         self.assertTrue(result.normal_text.strip().startswith("Some intro."))
 
+    def test_finish_releases_calls_that_completed_in_one_delta(self):
+        """Both calls in a single delta must reach the client.
+
+        A multi-token delta (speculative decoding / MTP, stream_interval > 1)
+        can carry more than one complete tool call. The incremental parser
+        leaves the tail of such a delta pending for the next delta; when the
+        stream ends there, the second call was dropped entirely and the first
+        arrived with empty arguments, while the non-streaming path returned
+        both.
+        """
+        text = (
+            '<|python_tag|>{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Paris"}}'
+            ';{"name": "get_tourist_attractions", "parameters": {"city": "Paris"}}'
+        )
+        detector = Llama32Detector()
+        chunk = detector.parse_streaming_increment(text, self.tools)
+        end = detector.finish(self.tools)
+        calls = list(chunk.calls) + list(end.calls)
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [call.name for call in calls if call.name],
+            ["get_weather", "get_tourist_attractions"],
+        )
+
+        streamed_args = {}
+        for call in calls:
+            streamed_args[call.tool_index] = streamed_args.get(call.tool_index, "") + (
+                call.parameters or ""
+            )
+        non_stream_args = {
+            call.tool_index: call.parameters
+            for call in Llama32Detector().detect_and_parse(text, self.tools).calls
+        }
+        self.assertEqual(len(non_stream_args), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(streamed_args, non_stream_args)
+
+    def test_finish_is_a_noop_when_nothing_is_pending(self):
+        text = '<|python_tag|>{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Paris"}}'
+        detector = Llama32Detector()
+        detector.parse_streaming_increment(text, self.tools)
+        detector.parse_streaming_increment("", self.tools)
+
+        end = detector.finish(self.tools)
+        self.assertEqual(end.calls, [])
+        self.assertEqual(end.normal_text, "")
+
+    def test_finish_releases_trailing_text_after_the_pending_calls(self):
+        """The drain must return both calls *and* the text still in the buffer.
+
+        A single multi-token delta can carry two complete calls plus trailing
+        prose. The calls are left pending by the one-unit-per-increment parser and
+        recovered by the drain; the trailing prose sits in the buffer and has to
+        come out as well, because ``detect_and_parse`` reports it for the same
+        input.
+        """
+        tools = [
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="get_weather",
+                    description="Get the weather",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
+                    },
+                ),
+            )
+        ]
+        text = (
+            '<|python_tag|>{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Paris"}}'
+            ';{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Rome"}} after'
+        )
+
+        detector = Llama32Detector()
+        chunk = detector.parse_streaming_increment(text, tools)
+        end = detector.finish(tools)
+
+        self.assertEqual(end.normal_text, " after")
+        merged, seen = {}, []
+        for call in list(chunk.calls or []) + list(end.calls or []):
+            if call.tool_index not in merged:
+                merged[call.tool_index] = [call.name, ""]
+                seen.append(call.tool_index)
+            if call.name:
+                merged[call.tool_index][0] = call.name
+            merged[call.tool_index][1] += call.parameters or ""
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [(merged[i][0], json.loads(merged[i][1])) for i in seen],
+            [
+                ("get_weather", {"city": "Paris"}),
+                ("get_weather", {"city": "Rome"}),
+            ],
+        )
+
 
 class TestKimiK2Detector(unittest.TestCase):
     def setUp(self):
